title: Salmon raises funds to double down in the Philippines
summary: Philippines-based banking and lending platform Salmon Group has raised $90 million in financing and another $50 million of bond proceeds.
content: Philippines-based banking and lending platform Salmon Group has successfully raised significant capital to expand its operations in the country. The company secured $90 million in financing along with an additional $50 million from bond proceeds. This fresh funding will enable Salmon to double down on its market strategy and further develop its financial services in the region.
content_ta: Philippines-வை தளமாகக் கொண்ட வங்கி மற்றும் கடன் வழங்கும் தளமான Salmon Group, தனது வணிகத்தை மேலும் விரிவுபடுத்துவதற்காக நிதி திரட்டியுள்ளது. இந்நிறுவனம் 90 மில்லியன் டாலர் நிதியுதவியையும், பத்திரங்கள் மூலம் கூடுதலாக 50 மில்லியன் டாலரையும் பெற்றுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய நிதி மூலம் Salmon தனது சந்தை உத்தியை வலுப்படுத்தி, அப்பகுதியில் தனது நிதி சேவைகளை மேலும் வளர்க்க முடியும்.

title: Stifel invests in Meow; preps white label treasury platform
summary: Stifel Financial has led a $31.6 million Series B finding round for business banking fintech Meow Technologies. The investment is part of a wider deal that will also see Stifel Bank offer a white-label version of Meow’s treasury management platform to its commercial banking clients.
content: Stifel Financial has led a $31.6 million Series B funding round for business banking fintech Meow Technologies. As part of the strategic investment, Stifel Bank will offer a white-label version of Meow's treasury management platform to its commercial banking clients, expanding financial services and banking technology capabilities.
content_ta: Stifel Financial நிறுவனம், பிசினஸ் பேங்கிங் ஃபின்டெக் நிறுவனமான Meow Technologies-க்கு $31.6 மில்லியன் சீரிஸ் B நிதி திரட்டலுக்கு தலைமை தாங்கியுள்ளது. இந்த முதலீட்டின் ஒரு பகுதியாக, Stifel Bank தனது வணிக வங்கிக் வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கு Meow-ன் கருவூல மேலாண்மை தளத்தின் ஒயிட்-லேபிள் பதிப்பை வழங்கவுள்ளது.

content: Fairlead's Katie Stockton has identified three warning signs that could potentially deepen the ongoing stock market selloff. title: EU will ban cash payments over €10,000 starting July 2027
summary:
The EU's cash payment cap aims to curb illicit financial activities, impacting high-value transactions and necessitating stricter compliance measures.
The post EU will ban cash payments over €10,000 starting July 2027 appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The European Union is set to implement a ban on cash payments exceeding €10,000 beginning in July 2027. This newly introduced cash payment cap is primarily designed to combat illicit financial activities across member states. The regulation will significantly impact high-value transactions and require businesses and consumers to adopt much stricter compliance measures moving forward.
content_ta: ஜூலை 2027 முதல் €10,000-க்கு மேற்பட்ட ரொக்கப் பணப் பரிவர்த்தனைகளுக்கு தடை விதிக்க EU திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது. சட்டவிரோத நிதி நடவடிக்கைகளைத் தடுப்பதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்ட இந்த புதிய ரொக்கப் பரிவர்த்தனை வரம்பு, உயர் மதிப்புடைய பரிவர்த்தனைகளைப் பாதிக்கும் மற்றும் கடுமையான இணக்க நடவடிக்கைகளைக் கோரும்.

title: Nasdaq rises as AI and semiconductor stocks recover ahead of earnings
summary:
The Nasdaq's recovery highlights investor optimism, but upcoming earnings will test if AI and semiconductor growth can sustain amid economic pressures.
The post Nasdaq rises as AI and semiconductor stocks recover ahead of earnings appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The Nasdaq index recently rose as artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks staged a recovery. This upward movement reflects renewed investor optimism in the technology sector. However, upcoming corporate earnings reports will serve as a crucial test to determine whether the current growth momentum in AI and semiconductor markets can be sustained against broader economic pressures.
content_ta: Nasdaq இன்டெக்ஸ் சமீபத்தில் AI மற்றும் செமிகண்டக்டர் பங்குகள் மீண்டெழுந்ததால் உயர்ந்தது. இந்த மேல்நோக்கிய இயக்கம் தொழில்நுட்பத் துறையில் முதலீட்டாளர்களின் புதிய நம்பிக்கையைப் பிரதிபலிக்கிறது. இருப்பினும், வரவிருக்கும் கார்ப்பரேட் வருவாய் அறிக்கைகள், பரந்த பொருளாதார அழுத்தங்களுக்கு மத்தியில் AI மற்றும் செமிகண்டக்டர் சந்தைகளின் தற்போதைய வளர்ச்சி வேகத்தைத் தக்க வைத்துக் கொள்ள முடியுமா என்பதைத் தீர்மானிக்க ஒரு முக்கியமான சோதனையாக இருக்கும்.

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman outlines three endgames for AI development
summary:
The outlined AI development paths highlight potential risks of power centralization, necessitating global cooperation for balanced progress.
The post OpenAI CEO Sam Altman outlines three endgames for AI development appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has outlined three potential endgames for artificial intelligence development. The discussion highlights the significant risks associated with the centralization of power in the tech industry. To ensure safe and balanced progress, Altman emphasizes the urgent need for global cooperation and careful navigation of future technological advancements.
content_ta: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, AI development-ன் மூன்று சாத்தியமான இறுதி நிலைகளை விளக்கியுள்ளார். தொழில்நுட்பத் துறையில் அதிகாரம் ஒரு இடத்திலேயே குவிக்கப்படுவதால் ஏற்படும் ஆபத்துகளை இது எடுத்துக்காட்டுகிறது. பாதுகாப்பான மற்றும் சீரான வளர்ச்சியை உறுதி செய்ய, உலகளாவிய ஒத்துழைப்பு மற்றும் எதிர்கால தொழில்நுட்ப முன்னேற்றங்களை கவனமாக கையாள்வது அவசியம் என்று அவர் வலியுறுத்துகிறார்.

title: CFTC secures more than $288 million order against former Long Island resident in Ponzi case
summary:
The ruling underscores the importance of due diligence for investors and reinforces regulatory efforts to deter financial misconduct.
The post CFTC secures more than $288 million order against former Long Island resident in Ponzi case appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The CFTC has secured an order exceeding $288 million against a former Long Island resident involved in a Ponzi scheme. This significant legal action highlights ongoing regulatory crackdowns on fraudulent financial activities and emphasizes the critical need for investor due diligence to prevent heavy losses in deceptive investment schemes.
content_ta: Ponzi வழக்கில் தொடர்புடைய Long Island-ஐச் சேர்ந்த முன்னாள் நபர் மீது $288 மில்லியனுக்கும் அதிகமான தொகையை அபராதமாக செலுத்த CFTC உத்தரவிட்டுள்ளது. இந்த முக்கிய சட்ட நடவடிக்கை நிதி மோசடிகளுக்கு எதிரான ஒழுங்குமுறை நடவடிக்கைகளை வலுப்படுத்துவதோடு, முதலீட்டாளர்கள் கவனமுடன் இருக்க வேண்டியதன் அவசியத்தையும் வலியுறுத்துகிறது.

content_ta: BNB Chain தங்களது புதிய Layer 1 ப்ராஜெக்ட் குறித்த சமூகத்தின் கருத்துக்களைப் பெற ஒரு புதிய ஆன்லைன் மன்றத்தைத் தொடங்கியுள்ளது. பிளாக்செயின் அளவிடுதல் மற்றும் பாதுகாப்பை மேம்படுத்துவதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்ட இந்த நெட்வொர்க்கை உருவாக்குவதில் டெவலப்பர்கள் மற்றும் பயனர்களை ஈர்ப்பதே இதன் நோக்கமாகும்.

title: Asia: Multilateral Lenders Advance Plans to Mobilise Private Capital, Expand Financing Capacity
summary: Multilateral development banks (MDBs) are stepping up efforts to attract private investment into emerging markets and increase their lending capacity as developing economies face mounting debt pressures, economic uncertainty, and climate-related disasters. The heads of the world’s major multilateral lenders met at the Asian Development... Read More
content: Major multilateral development banks are advancing plans to mobilize private capital and expand their financing capacity in emerging markets. Meeting in Asia, leaders of these institutions are responding to growing economic uncertainties, severe debt pressures, and climate-related disasters faced by developing economies, aiming to significantly boost investment and financial support.
content_ta: வளர்ந்து வரும் பொருளாதாரங்கள் எதிர்கொள்ளும் கடுமையான கடன் நெருக்கடிகள், பொருளாதார நிச்சயமற்ற தன்மைகள் மற்றும் பருவநிலை சார்ந்த பேரிடர்களைச் சமாளிக்க, முக்கிய MDBs தனியார் முதலீடுகளை ஈர்ப்பதற்கான திட்டங்களையும் தங்களின் நிதி வழங்கும் திறனை விரிவுபடுத்துவதற்கும் தீவிர நடவடிக்கைகளை எடுத்து வருகின்றன. ஆசியாவில் நடைபெற்ற இக்கூட்டத்தில், உலகின் முக்கிய பல்தரப்பு கடன் வழங்குநர்களின் தலைவர்கள் பங்கேற்றனர்.

title: Bitcoin rally could revive treasury buying, but easy-money days over
summary: “A return to last year’s indiscriminate capital raising looks unlikely,” said Bitfinex head of derivatives Jag Kooner.
content: A recent Bitcoin rally may encourage firms to resume treasury buying, though the era of easy money has ended. Analysts note that a return to last year's indiscriminate capital raising remains unlikely, indicating a more cautious approach to market expansion moving forward.
content_ta: சமீபத்திய Bitcoin விலை உயர்வு நிறுவனங்களை மீண்டும் கருவூல கொள்முதலில் ஈடுபடத் தூண்டலாம், இருப்பினும் எளிதான பண காலம் முடிவுக்கு வந்துவிட்டது. கடந்த ஆண்டைப் போல கண்மூடித்தனமாக நிதி திரட்டுவது இனி சாத்தியமில்லை என்றும், சந்தை விரிவாக்கத்தில் நிறுவனங்கள் மிகவும் எச்சரிக்கையுடன் செயல்படும் என்றும் ஆய்வாளர்கள் குறிப்பிடுகின்றனர்.

title: Binance opens free AI trading, yet user liability remains 100%
summary:

content: Binance has launched a free AI trading tool offering monthly usage credits and live deployment capabilities. While the platform provides the technology, users must supply their own trading funds and approve workflows. title: Why Citi Thinks Microsoft Beats Neoclouds in the AI Debt Squeeze
summary:
Citi's Tyler Radke blames bond yields, not weak demand, for the neocloud selloff and backs Microsoft instead.
The post Why Citi Thinks Microsoft Beats Neoclouds in the AI Debt Squeeze appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Zoho Launches Payroll Solution in the UK to Handle PAYE, National Insurance Calculations and RTI Submissions
summary:
Zoho Corporation, the global technology company, has launched Zoho Payroll, a payroll management solution built around the compliance requirements of UK businesses.
The solution handles Pay As You Earn (PAYE) and National Insurance calculations, as well as Real Time Information (RTI) submissions to HMRC. Zoho Payroll also comes with built-in AI capabilities, like Ask Zia Zoho's AI assistant tool, which payroll teams can use to complete tasks, generate forecasts and identify trends, using plain-language prompts. The AI assistant can also answer employees' payroll questions.
"Payroll is a critical component of the employee experience, so getting it right is important," said Prashant Ganti, VP of Global Product Strategy, Finance and Operations Business Unit, Zoho. "However, payroll doesn't happen in isolation, and because it shares sensitive employee data with other systems, any gap is a compliance risk and a privacy risk. Zoho Payroll offers built-in compliance, with privacy at its core, helping businesses always stay compliant as the rules evolve while keeping their employee data secure. Furthermore, the solution brings payroll, HR, employee expenses and accounting together in a smooth flow, so that businesses can pay their employees accurately and on time."
UK payroll is undergoing a significant period of regulatory change in recent years. Since April 2026, Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is payable from the first day of sickness. More changes are expected to be implemented from April 2027 such as benefits in kind which must be taxed through payroll for each pay period instead of reporting it on P11D forms. Moreover, a full payment submission must be made to HMRC on or before payday, and late filing can attract monthly penalties starting at £100 for businesses with up to nine employees.
All these regulatory changes add to the existing compliance obligations of businesses making it more challenging for them to keep up. In fact, findings from a recent study done by Finity, show that 89% of payroll professionals said they had run into payment errors in the past year, and 38% said problems arise every month. Many of these avoidable errors stem from manual processes and disconnected systems, and this is the exact gap that Zoho Payroll is built to close.
The solution's key capabilities include:
● RTI reporting: a Full Payment Submission (FPS) generated for every pay run, and Employer Payment Summary (EPS) submissions where required.
● Statutory payments and deductions: All statutory payments such as Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP) and Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) based on employee eligibility can be managed seamlessly. The solution supports deductions like student loan repayments, Attachment of Earnings (AoE), Benefits in Kind (BiK), and P45 forms for employees leaving the organisation.
● Workplace pensions: businesses can run eligibility checks, auto-enrol eligible employees, handle opt-ins and opt-outs, and postpone pension enrolment when required.
● Payroll administration: employers can manage multiple work locations, with fine-grained role-based access, run activity logs, and set up payroll reminders
● Employee self-service: employees can review payslips, tax summaries and pension information through the self-service portal, available on web and mobile.
● Reporting: P11, P32 and payroll summary reports can be generated, and export them as PDF, XLS or CSV, with password-protected sharing.

title: LHV Bank Goes Live With AI Agent for Customer Emails, Powered by Gradient Labs
summary:
LHV Bank has gone live with agentic AI for customer email support in the UK, powered by Gradient Labs. The launch follows a proof of concept announced earlier this year and means LHV’s retail customers can now get immediate answers to everyday banking questions by email, around the clock.
The AI agent handles common enquiries from start to finish, such as what to do about a lost card, an explanation of a payment, transfer queries, or what happens next with an existing request. Cases that are sensitive, complex or outside the agent’s approved procedures are passed to LHV’s customer support team.
Faster answers, more time for complex cases
Like other banks, LHV Bank's traditional queue-based approach to customer queries didn't distinguish between simple questions and complex ones. With this launch, simple queries get immediate answers, freeing up LHV's team to focus on the cases where human judgement matters most.
How it works
AI agent handles scoped journeys: Using Gradient Labs, LHV Bank's AI agent resolves clearly defined customer journeys from start to finish.
Works within set limits: The agent operates only within approved procedures, tools and controls.
Humans set the rules: LHV's teams define each process, its boundaries and what the agent is allowed to do.
Humans approve changes: Any updates are tested and signed off by LHV’s team before going live.
Ongoing oversight: LHV monitors quality and handles any exceptions the agent escalates.
Guardrails built for regulated banking
As LHV Bank operates in a regulated environment, its AI agent pairs large language models with deterministic guardrails. These control what data and tools the agent can access, when actions are blocked or escalated, and how complaints and vulnerable customers are handled. Customer data is never used to train the models, or build the agent, and is accessed only during live interactions.
Improving the agent like software
LHV Bank is also using Collaborate, part of the Gradient Labs platform, which applies software engineering discipline to customer-facing AI. LHV’s operations, product, engineering, risk and compliance teams can draft changes to the agent’s procedures in a controlled branch, test them against representative customer cases, review and approve them before they reach customers, and roll them back if needed. Every change carries a clear record of what changed, who approved it and when, so the service can improve continuously without the bank losing control of it.
What’s next?
LHV Bank’s immediate focus is to extend the agent to more customer servicing procedures within UK email support. Longer term, the two companies will explore further channels such as live chat and voice, back-office and financial crime workflows including onboarding, KYC and AML, and potential expansion into LHV’s Estonian business.

Dimitri Masin, CEO of Gradient Labs, added: 
“The future of AI in financial services is not a faster human approving AI suggestions at every step. It is trusted agents taking responsibility for defined work, supported by deterministic controls, clear escalation points and human judgement where it matters. LHV is showing what that can look like in practice.”

title: New Research Shows How AI Will Change the Gift Card Industry
summary:
Blackhawk Network (BHN), a global branded payments leader, today released new research surveying 694 U.S. business leaders responsible for incentives, commerce and branded payments, finding that artificial intelligence could fundamentally change how consumers discover, select and purchase gift cards. The findings are pertinent as businesses prepare for a future where AI assistants will act on a shopper’s behalf.
 
According to BHN's AI & Branded Payments Study, 42% of the payments leaders surveyed believe that by 2030, AI will most likely reshape consumers' path to purchasing gift cards through an AI concierge. This assistant will recommend a gift card, select the value and send it—without the consumer ever visiting the retailer's website or app. Another 32% expect AI will recommend gift cards based on a recipient's interests, past purchases and preferences, while 24% expect AI assistants to purchase and deliver the right gift card for preapproved occasions.
 

“AI has the potential to change not only how consumers find the right gift, but how that purchase ultimately gets made,” said Talbott Roche, CEO and president of BHN. “As AI assistants take a more active role in shopping, brands will need to consider how they remain discoverable, relevant and connected to customers when agents are helping determine what gets purchased.”
 
Businesses are already beginning to prepare for that shift. Twenty-three percent of the payments leaders surveyed said they are building or piloting for agentic commerce, while another 47% are actively exploring what it means for their branded payments programs. Twenty-two percent are aware of agentic commerce but have not yet taken action, while just 8% said they are not thinking about it yet.
 
The findings suggest AI could also emerge as a new distribution channel for branded payments. Additionally, AI will more effectively integrate gift cards into shoppers’ lives. For instance, an AI assistant could surface an existing gift card when a consumer is shopping at a relevant retailer, or proactively suggest an appropriate gift card and budget for an upcoming loved one’s special occasion. As AI assistants become capable of moving consumers from recommendation to purchase within a single interaction, brands will need to make gift cards and stored value easier for AI systems to find, understand and confidently recommend.
 

“For brands, the broader opportunity is to make stored value more useful in the moments when consumers are ready to act, while still giving them transparency and control over the experience,” Roche said.
 
Thirty-five percent of businesses surveyed also identified customer experience as an area where they expect AI to have the greatest impact on branded payments by 2030. The research found businesses are looking for better data and analytics and more personalized gifting experiences as they consider how to put AI to work within their programs.

title: BlackRock Files For Bitcoin ETF With Managed Downside Protection
summary: TL;DR: BlackRock has proposed another Bitcoin-linked ETF, this time using options to pursue some protection against losses while giving up part of the potential upside. BlackRock’s latest Bitcoin fund filing takes a different approach from the familiar buy-and-hold exposure offered by its iShares Bitcoin Trust. Instead of simply following the price of Bitcoin, the proposed iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF would use an options strategy linked to IBIT or similar exposure. The ambition is straightforward enough: participate in some of Bitcoin’s gains and seek a measure of protection during a decline. The trade-off is equally important. Gains could be capped, and the protection is neither unconditional nor guaranteed. The structure is designed around overlapping options positions, meaning an investor’s outcome could depend on when the shares are purchased as well as what Bitcoin does next. That makes this a different kind of product, not a safer version of holding spot Bitcoin in every circumstance. Options costs, fund expenses and changing market prices all affect what shareholders receive. The filing arrives as issuers work to move beyond basic spot exposure. Income-oriented and buffered Bitcoin products try to give financial advisers additional ways to fit an unusually volatile asset into conventional portfolios. For investors, the missing details matter as much as the proposed strategy. An SEC filing does not mean the fund has been approved or launched. Its eventual fees, live portfolio and actual protection terms will determine whether the structure delivers a useful alternative to IBIT. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Two in Five Financial Services Leaders Say AI Capability Gaps Have Cost Them Business
summary:
​​​Two in five (40%) financial services directors and C-Suite professionals say their organisation has lost a competitive bid or client opportunity partly because of AI capability concerns, according to new research from Kaplan UK - a leading provider of professional education, apprenticeship training, and enterprise upskilling.
The findings suggest that capability gaps are beginning to have a direct commercial impact in a sector where AI adoption is already a significant strategic priority.
More than four in five (81%) C-Suite respondents in financial services told Kaplan that AI adoption and expansion is a high or top organisational priority over the next 12 months, compared with 74% of leaders across industries overall.
Financial services C-Suite teams were also more likely to say they are confident their organisation has a clearly defined AI strategy that is understood at senior level.
However, Kaplan’s research suggests investment in the sector remains more heavily weighted towards technology than the workforce expected to use it.
Half (50%) of financial services C-Suite respondents said their organisation has placed greater emphasis on investing in AI tools and technology, compared with just 17% who said greater emphasis has been placed on workforce capability development.
The findings are published in Kaplan’s new whitepaper, From AI to ROI: Who owns the problem? which examines the relationship between AI investment, workforce capability and business performance. The Kaplan study is grounded in the views of 1,000 UK employees, 600 HR and L&D professionals, and 600 company directors and C-Suite leaders.
Financial services leaders also estimated that fewer than half of the employees (45%) expected to work with AI are genuinely proficient, compared to 79% of employees in the sector that are confident in using AI productively.
Taken together, the findings point to a potential gap between strategic ambition and organisations’ ability to translate AI investment into day-to-day capability. Despite high levels of leadership focus on AI, many financial services businesses are investing more heavily in the technology itself than in developing the people expected to apply it.
​​​Chiraag Swaly, Head of Data and Technology Curriculum at Kaplan, said: “Financial services organisations clearly recognise the strategic importance of AI. The sector is prioritising adoption and leaders are putting AI strategies in place, but the research suggests that technology investment alone is not enough to generate a return.
“When four in ten C-Suite leaders say AI capability concerns have contributed to losing a bid or client opportunity, workforce capability becomes a commercial issue rather than simply a training issue.
“Financial services employees operate in environments where judgement, accuracy and the appropriate use of technology matter enormously. Giving people access to AI is therefore only one part of the challenge. Organisations also need to ensure employees can apply those tools effectively in the context of their roles.
“The gap between investment in technology and investment in workforce capability is significant. Closing it will require organisations to treat the skills needed to use AI as part of the transformation itself, rather than something that follows deployment.”
The findings reflect a broader pattern identified by Kaplan across UK businesses. While organisations are investing heavily in AI, the research suggests workforce development is not always progressing at the same pace.
Across industries, 54% of C-Suite and director respondents said AI-related investment has placed greater emphasis on tools and technology than workforce capability development, while only 20% say the greater emphasis has been on developing employees’ skills.
Kaplan argues that the challenge for financial services organisations is therefore not simply to accelerate AI adoption, but to ensure investment in technology is matched by the practical capability needed to use it effectively across the workforce.

summary: TL;DR: BlackRock’s IBIT recorded roughly $665 million in net inflows on October 19, even as several other US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw investors take money out. The reversal also follows a Friday session in which the group recorded net withdrawals. It underscores how quickly flows can shift around market volatility and broader risk sentiment. Flows are useful evidence of ETF subscriptions and redemptions, but they shouldn’t be read as a direct measure of new cash buying Bitcoin at a particular hour. Fund mechanics and market-making activity complicate that picture. The next question is whether demand spreads to other products or whether IBIT continues to absorb most of the market’s incremental interest. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

summary: TL;DR: Mesh and Visa have announced a partnership intended to let consumers spend cryptocurrency and stablecoins from participating wallet apps wherever Visa payments are accepted. title: Mastercard Introduces Risk Intelligence to Enable More Secure Stablecoin Payments
summary:
Today at Money20/20 USA, Mastercard announced Stablecoin Security, a new risk intelligence solution, with Borderless.xyz and Keyrails as initial partners. As stablecoins play a growing role in cross-border and business-to-business payments, financial institutions need a clearer view of risk across increasingly complex payment flows. The solution builds on Mastercard’s existing capabilities and helps financial institutions identify fraud, scams, sanctions and other financial-crime risk indicators throughout the stablecoin payment lifecycle, including before funds move on-chain.
Why do financial institutions need better stablecoin risk intelligence? 
A study of 593 million stablecoin transfer events across 141 million Ethereum transactions in 2025 found that nearly 60% were complex, multi-step transactions, rather than simple, one-to-one payments. This can make it harder for financial institutions to assess risk across the full payment journey, from supplier payments and global trade settlement to moving funds across countries and currencies. Stablecoin Security helps close that gap by combining payment intelligence with blockchain analytics, giving financial institutions a more complete view of risk at key points in the transaction lifecycle.
“Stablecoins are creating new possibilities for value exchange, but financial institutions need the right intelligence and controls to participate with confidence,” said Ann Johnson, executive vice president, Security Solutions at Mastercard. “By bringing payment and blockchain insights together, Stablecoin Security extends Mastercard’s fraud and risk capabilities to digital asset payments, giving institutions a clearer view of risk to make more informed decisions and build greater trust.”
How does Stablecoin Security work? 
Delivered through a platform-agnostic application programming interface (API), Stablecoin Security analyzes signals including transaction context, where the funds came from, exposure to restricted parties and scam indicators. It generates intelligence across the fiat and stablecoin payment lifecycle, including a risk score before a payment is completed, and can be integrated into existing fraud, compliance and case management workflows. This allows financial institutions to support stablecoin payments without creating a separate risk operating model.
For example, consider a coffee shop owner in Boston purchasing coffee beans from a supplier in Brazil. The coffee shop initiates payment through its bank, which uses stablecoins to move funds across borders more quickly and efficiently. Before the payment is sent, the bank’s service provider uses Mastercard Stablecoin Security to analyze payment and blockchain intelligence, helping the bank determine whether the payment can proceed as expected or should be reviewed further. The Brazilian supplier receives the funds and confidently converts the stablecoin to local currency.
Partnering across the stablecoin ecosystem to scale 
Mastercard is working with Borderless.xyz and Keyrails, both participants in Mastercard’s Start Path Blockchain and Digital Assets startup engagement program, to bring Stablecoin Security to real-world payment flows. Keyrails supports high-value cross-border trade payments, particularly in emerging markets. Borderless.xyz gives financial institutions a single connection to licensed stablecoin providers in more than 113 countries and 72 currencies, handles the operations behind every payment, and enables routing each one to the best provider. In 2027, Mastercard will continue to expand Stablecoin Security’s reach and adoption, including through BVNK, the stablecoin infrastructure provider it acquired in August 2026.
Stablecoin Security builds on Mastercard's broader efforts to bring trust, security and transparency to stablecoin and digital asset transactions. Alongside complementary capabilities such as Mastercard Crypto Credential and Crypto Secure, it aims to help financial institutions navigate emerging forms of money movement with greater confidence. 
The solution is launching first in North America, with commercial availability expected worldwide in 2027.

title: August Breaks UK Credit Card Record as Balances Soar
summary:
According to data analysis from global analytics software leader FICO, average active UK credit card balances exceeded £2,000 in August for the first time since records began, following three consecutive months of increases. Contributing to higher balances, payment rates dropped after a brief recovery in July, and remain lower than the same time last year. This trend, coupled with an annual increase in all levels of missed payments, highlights the importance of risk teams continuing to closely monitor for signs of financial difficulty.
Highlights
Average spending increased by 3.1% month-on-month to £840, growing 3.3% year-on-year and marking the highest annual growth rate in over a year.
The average active balance grew 1.2% month-on-month to a record £2,005 and remains up 4.8% year-on-year.
The percentage of overall balance paid fell 1.1% on the previous month, to 33.3%, and is down 3.1% year-on-year.
Average credit limits crossed £6,000 for the first time, and overlimit accounts grew 4.7% month-on-month to an average overlimit of £95. This is down -3.1% on the previous month but up 3.3% year-on-year.
The percentage of customers missing one payment fell by 7.1% month-on-month but balances for these accounts rose 5.1% year-on-year, to £2,520.
Accounts with two missed payments climbed 2.8% compared to July, but are 9.5% higher year-on-year. Annual growth for balances of these accounts slowed to 1.8%, with the average standing at £2,945.
There was a slight monthly decline of 0.7% in three missed payments, but year-on-year there was a sharp increase of 16.4%. Average balances grew 1.7% on the year, reaching £3,320.
FICO Comment:
August marked significant milestones, as average active balances passed £2,000 and credit limits exceeded £6,000 for the first time. The year-on-year shortfall in payment rates narrowed for a third consecutive month, while overlimit accounts showed year-on-year improvement. This suggests that acute affordability pressures from earlier in the year are beginning to ease slightly, despite the persistent pressure on finances that has characterised the market since early 2025. However, late payments across all three cycles remain higher than in 2025, reflecting a macroeconomic environment that continues to stretch household budgets.
UK CPI inflation rose to 3.1% in August, up from 2.9% in July, driven in part by rising food prices. With Ofgem’s energy price cap set to increase, borrowing costs are unlikely to fall significantly before winter. Meanwhile, total UK credit card debt has reached a record £82.4 billion according to the Bank of England, alongside record-high representative credit card interest rates.
Given these cost pressures, risk teams should monitor whether the recent stability in payment rates and overlimit accounts can be sustained. Although one-cycle delinquency fell sharply in August, it remains 5.1% higher year-on-year. As the primary entry point to the delinquency pipeline, and with CPI and energy costs both rising into autumn, early intervention and tailored support for this population should be prioritised before further seasonal pressure builds

content: UK credit card balances exceeded £2,000 for the first time in August, according to FICO data, driven by rising spending and falling payment rates. Average credit limits also crossed £6,000. While some affordability pressures eased slightly, missed payments remained higher year-on-year amid ongoing economic challenges, including rising inflation and energy costs.
content_ta: FICO-வின் தரவுகளின்படி, ஆகஸ்ட் மாதத்தில் UK-ல் கிரெடிட் கார்டு நிலுவைத் தொகைகள் முதல்முறையாக £2,000-ஐத் தாண்டின. அதிகரித்த செலவினங்களும் குறைந்த செலுத்தல் விகிதங்களும் இதற்குக் காரணமாகும். சராசரி கிரெடிட் வரம்புகளும் £6,500-ஐத் தாண்டியுள்ளன. பொருளாதார சவால்கள் தொடரும் நிலையில், கட்டணம் செலுத்தத் தவறியவர்களின் எண்ணிக்கை சென்ற ஆண்டைக் காட்டிலும் அதிகமாகவே உள்ளது.
